scenes.heading: Inference
scenes.sub: Reading what the writer shows but never says
scenes.say: Writers don't always tell you things directly. They leave clues. Inference questions check whether you can read those clues and work out what's really going on.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: You see smoke, so you know there's a fire
scenes.science: You read clues, so you know what the text means
scenes.breaks: smoke could come from a barbecue; in the test, pick the conclusion that fits every clue.
scenes.say: You see smoke rising from behind a hill. You can't see the fire, but you know it's there. That's inference. But be careful: smoke could be a barbecue. In the test, choose the conclusion that fits every clue.

scenes.heading: The inference formula
parts: words or actions in the text
scenes.say: Here's the formula. Clue, plus what I know, equals inference. The clue comes from the text. What you know comes from everyday life. Together they give you the answer.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Sam chews his pencil, re-reads question one three times and wipes his sweaty palms. How does he feel?
lines: Know: these are signs of stress
scenes.say: Sam chews his pencil, reads the first question three times, checks the clock and wipes his sweaty palms. Those clues, plus what you know about stress, tell you he's nervous, not bored.

scenes.heading: Must be true vs could be true

right.title: Could be true
points: Needs a long chain of maybes

scenes.say: The trap answer is often something that could be true in real life, but has no clue in the passage. Choose the answer the clues force you to believe, and make sure it fits every clue.

scenes.heading: How to answer
scenes.say: So, collect two or three clues. Add what you know. Cross out options with no clue. Then check your answer fits every clue, not just one.

points: Must be true, not could be true
Fit every clue; take a small step
scenes.say: Quick recap. An inference is something the text shows but doesn't say. Clue plus what I know equals inference. Choose what must be true, check every clue, and stay close to the text. Now try the practice questions!
